# Pet voice — lessons

The top block is regenerated by `python3 pet_voice.py learn` from every receipt in
`evidence/`. It also writes `learned/voice-scores.json`, which the next `talk`/`relay`
reads: model order (working, fastest first), the accepted TTS request shape per model and
voice×language intelligibility (`--adapt` swaps a voice that listeners keep mis-hearing).
The curated section below is for lessons a script cannot infer — add one line per new lesson.

## Curated lessons

- **Use the MBP Keychain key directly in-process.** `gemini-agent` deliberately refuses
  generation (`status|inventory|probe` only); voice work uses `pet_voice.py`, which reads the
  same Keychain item with `/usr/bin/security` and never prints it. (2026-11-14)
- **Check the live model list, not memory.** `gemini-2.5-flash-lite` returned 404 for this
  project although listed; 3.8 TTS/text models worked. `learn` drops 403/404/per-day-quota
  models from the order automatically. (2026-11-14)
- **Newest is not fastest.** On 14 Nov `gemini-3.8-flash` stalled >2 min on an audio+JSON
  listen request while `gemini-3.5-flash` answered in ~8 s (transcript accuracy 0.98) and
  `gemini-3.5-flash-lite` in ~3 s (same accuracy, but it skipped "address the next pet by
  name"). Calls now time out (45 s listen / 90 s TTS) and fall through to the next model;
  `learn` counts timeouts as failures. (2026-11-14)
- **Background jobs over RDC die with the call.** `cmd &` inside `start_process` was killed;
  run long relays in a named tmux session via the RDC `session.py` helper. (2026-11-14)
- **Two speakers max per Gemini TTS request**, so multi-agent talk is synthesized per turn;
  that also keeps every pet's own voice and makes runs resumable per turn. (2026-11-14)
- **Measure intelligibility, don't guess it.** The listener only receives audio; comparing
  its transcript with what the speaker meant to say gives a free per-voice, per-language
  quality signal on every turn. (2026-11-14)
